quartodown builds a website for an R package with [Quarto](https://quarto.org/).
This guide sets up a package, builds its site, and publishes it on GitHub Pages.

## Set up

From the root of your package, run:

```r
quartodown::use_quartodown()
```

This writes `_quartodown.yml` at the package root, the configuration file you
can edit, and adds the files the build generates to `.gitignore` and
`.Rbuildignore`.

## Build the site

```r
quartodown::build_site()
quartodown::preview_site()
```

`build_site()` builds the site into `docs/`, and `preview_site()` opens it in
your browser. Examples and vignettes run against your package's current source.
While iterating, `build_site(devel = TRUE)` is faster because it loads the
package with `pkgload::load_all()` instead of installing it.

The following is added to your site:

- **Home page**: your `README.md`. Next to it, a sidebar links to the source
  code, the bug tracker and CRAN (if the package is there), and shows the
  license, citation and authors from `DESCRIPTION`. Any badges in your README
  (between `<!-- badges: start -->` and `<!-- badges: end -->`) are moved into
  the sidebar.
- **Reference**: a page for each help topic in `man/`, plus an index page
  listing them all.
- **Get started**: the vignette with the same name as your package, like this
  one.
- **Articles**: all your other vignettes, including any in
  `vignettes/articles/`.
- **Changelog**: your `NEWS.md`. Issue numbers like `#123` and GitHub usernames
  like `@user` become links.

## Organize the reference index

By default the reference index lists every function in one section. To group
them, edit the `reference:` field in `_quartodown.yml`. It has the same shape as
pkgdown's:

```yaml
reference:
  - title: Setting up
    contents:
      - use_quartodown
  - title: Building
    contents:
      - starts_with("build_")
```

See `?build_site` for the other fields.

## Publish on GitHub Pages

To build the site and deploy it to the `gh-pages` branch on every push, add a
GitHub Actions workflow:

```r
quartodown::use_quartodown_action()
```

This writes `.github/workflows/quartodown.yaml`. Commit and push it. Once its
first run has created the `gh-pages` branch, go to the *Pages* section of your
repository's settings on GitHub and choose to deploy from that branch.

## Learn more

[Technical
details](https://bjarkehautop.github.io/quartodown/vignettes/articles/technical.html)
explains how a build works and how quartodown's theme is put together.
